## Acceptance Criteria

Fail. The scanner is deterministic on this repo, but it does not evaluate every canonical content-standard rule, and it accepts malformed `REQ-NN` criteria.

## Architecture And Separation

Fail. The new scanner reads `.jit/issues/*.json` directly from a skill shell script instead of going through the storage abstraction.

## Functional Paradigm

Pass. No Rust implementation was added, and the shell script is mostly linear data extraction.

## Correctness And Invariants

Fail. No atomic writes, event writes, gate transitions, assignee parsing, label parsing, or PID code were added. The blocking correctness issues are scanner coverage and malformed criterion detection.

## Safety

Pass. No unsafe Rust was added.

## Testing

Fail. `./scripts/jit-validate.sh` passed with label warnings only. I also verified the scanner emits byte-identical output on two unchanged runs. There is no committed test/golden fixture coverage for the new scanner.

## Error Handling

Pass for the script surface. Bad invocation and missing tool cases exit with contextual errors.

## CLI Contract

Pass. No Rust CLI command surface changed.

## Documentation

Partial pass. The reference doc describes the script and JSONL schema, but it also documents the same incomplete rule catalog implemented by the script.

## Prior Review Feedback

`run_history` is empty, so there were no prior findings to verify.

## Jit Issue Management

`./scripts/jit-validate.sh` passed. The listed dependency `87c8ba2d` is marked done in the provided issue context.

1. `.claude/skills/jit-project-lead/scripts/standards-scan.sh:86-95` reads `.jit/issues/*.json` directly with `jq`, and `.claude/skills/jit-project-lead/scripts/standards-scan.sh:223-225` reads issue title/description directly from JSON. That violates the repository boundary that persistence must sit behind `IssueStore`; this is new technical debt in the scanner path.

2. `.claude/skills/jit-project-lead/scripts/standards-scan.sh:174` accepts `REQ-[0-9]+`, so `[hard] REQ-1:` is treated as well-formed. The issue requires malformed `[hard]`/`[aspirational]` `REQ-NN` criteria to be classified as mechanical findings.

3. `.claude/skills/jit-project-lead/scripts/standards-scan.sh:184-190` does not evaluate every rule in `docs/reference/jit-content-standards.md`. For example, the math rules require variable names in math mode and `\frac{a}{b}` for display fractions (`docs/reference/jit-content-standards.md:148-150`), but the scanner misses text like `x` outside math mode or `a/b`.

4. There are no committed tests for the new scanner. The change adds `.claude/skills/jit-project-lead/scripts/standards-scan.sh` and `.claude/skills/jit-project-lead/references/standards-scan.md`, but no shell test, fixture, or golden-output test covering the required mechanical cases, judgment cases, scope filtering, or determinism.
